doc: Extra objectives a mission can pursue. When a mission starts, three are drawn at random from those of its scenario and the team chooses which to go for; each one met adds its points and never takes any away. `check` says what the flight must do (kinds are read by scripts/flight/objectives.gd): `target_m`, `pole_m`, `shadow_edge_m` (distance in metres at touchdown, at most `max`), `touchdown_mps` (touchdown speed, at most `max`), `fuel_left` (share of the lander's fuel left, at least `min`), `contact_kept` (Earth in view through the whole descent), `correction_dv` (m/s of the mid-course correction, at most `max`), `ascent_error_deg` (mean degrees off the guidance marker on the climb, at most `max`). `photo` is the picture the mission sends home when the objective is met. Ids are stable keys, never shown to players. Objectives with scenario `any_orbit` serve every mission that has no landing of its own: `ascent_fuel_left` (share of the last stage's fuel left in orbit, at least `min`), `science_frac` (science gathered over the mission's goal, at least `min`), `budget_reserve` (share of the budget left, at least `min`).

shadow_photo.name: Look into the dark
shadow_photo.desc: Land within 300 m of the edge of the permanent shadow and photograph the crater floor that has not seen the Sun for billions of years, the way ShadowCam does from orbit.
shadow_photo.how: Pick a landing target next to the dark crater floor, then steer with the arrows to touch down within 300 m of the shadow's edge.
shadow_photo.simplified: The 300 m and the points are our game values; the photo is ShadowCam's real picture of Shackleton's floor.

rim_landing.name: Bullseye on the rim
rim_landing.desc: Touch down within 60 m of the target on Shackleton's sunlit rim, where the Sun shines almost all month long.
rim_landing.how: In the landing, follow the green ring: steer with the arrows and touch down within 60 m of it (the autopilot aims for it too).
rim_landing.simplified: The 60 m and the points are our game values.

earth_contact.name: Never lose Earth
earth_contact.desc: Keep Earth in view of the antenna through the whole descent. From the pole Earth hangs low on the horizon, so a hill or the crater wall can hide it.
earth_contact.how: Choose a landing spot on the high rim, not in a hollow, so no hill hides the Earth during the descent.
earth_contact.simplified: Earth's height above the horizon is fixed at 3 degrees in the game; it really wobbles a few degrees over the month. The hills that hide it are the real LOLA heights.

soft_touch.name: Feather touch
soft_touch.desc: Touch down slower than 1.5 m/s, gently enough not to spill a cup of coffee.
soft_touch.how: In the last metres hold W for more throttle until the speed shows under 1.5 m/s, or press Space to hover and sink slowly.
soft_touch.simplified: The 1.5 m/s is our game value. Touchdown speed and the slope under the legs are what decide a landing [S-apollo-gear].

fuel_hop.name: Fuel for a hop
fuel_hop.desc: Land with a third of the lander's fuel left. Chandrayaan-3's lander used its spare fuel to rise 40 cm and land again a little farther on.
fuel_hop.how: Land without long hovers: fly straight down to the ring and brake late with W, so a third of the fuel is still in the tank.
fuel_hop.simplified: The share of fuel and the points are our game values.

pole_visit.name: The bottom of the world
pole_visit.desc: Touch down within 250 m of the geographic south pole, 90 degrees south, the spot every line of longitude meets.
pole_visit.how: Pick the landing target closest to the pole marker and steer with the arrows to touch down within 250 m of it.
pole_visit.simplified: The pole's place is where the LOLA map's projection puts it; the 250 m and the points are our game values.

true_burn.name: Bullseye departure
true_burn.desc: Keep a departure so well planned that the correction on the way stays under 60 m/s: moving the burn away from the best moment costs far more.
true_burn.how: In the trip, give the GO (Space) on the planned departure without moving it: the closer to the best moment, the smaller the correction.
true_burn.simplified: The 60 m/s and the points are our game values. The game plans the departure as one instant kick and the real burn lasts six minutes, so its correction is larger than Apollo's.

ride_marker.name: Ride the marker
ride_marker.desc: Fly the climb yourself and keep the rocket within 5 degrees of the guidance marker, on average, all the way to orbit.
ride_marker.how: In the launch, take the controls and lean with ← → to keep the needle on the green marker all the way to orbit.
ride_marker.simplified: The 5 degrees and the points are our game values.

fly_climb.name: Fly the climb yourself
fly_climb.desc: Take the stick for most of the climb and keep the needle within 6 degrees of the green marker on average, as a pilot does on a real launch.
fly_climb.how: In the launch, take the controls (touch ← →) and keep the needle on the green marker for most of the climb.
fly_climb.simplified: The 6 degrees and the points are our game values.

fuel_spare.name: Reach orbit with fuel to spare
fuel_spare.desc: Arrive in orbit with at least 5 % of the last stage's fuel left: a clean climb wastes nothing.
fuel_spare.how: Choose a launcher with payload to spare for your craft, and in the climb keep the needle on the marker: zig-zags burn fuel.
fuel_spare.simplified: The 5 % and the points are our game values.

science_goal.name: Hit the science goal
science_goal.desc: Gather all the science points the mission asks for: enough power, a fast enough antenna and the right instruments.
science_goal.how: In the design, pick the instruments the mission asks for and enough panels and antenna, until the Science line of the mission board turns green.
science_goal.simplified: The points are our game values.

reserve.name: Keep a quarter of the budget
reserve.desc: Finish with at least 25 % of the budget left over, the reserve real agencies love to see.
reserve.how: In the design, keep the cost bar under three quarters of the budget: a smaller platform or a cheaper launcher saves the most.
reserve.simplified: The 25 % and the points are our game values; real missions keep 10 to 30 % for surprises.
